rendering.persona_description: Mercedes is a 24-year-old who works as a veterinary technician at a busy small-animal clinic. She grew up the oldest of three kids and has always been the one people call for a straight answer, which she likes being. She reads a lot of true crime and thinks of herself as someone who pays close attention to details other people miss.
rendering.clinical_context: Mercedes has obsessive-compulsive disorder centered on intrusive thoughts and images of harming animals in her care, especially the ones she sedates and handles alone, which she experiences as evidence of a real and present danger in herself rather than as unwanted mental noise. She has spent long stretches checking equipment, replaying procedures in her head, and asking coworkers to confirm she did things correctly. She saw a therapist for several months after her sister pushed her to, but stopped going about a year ago and has not been in treatment since.
rendering.behavioral_description: Mercedes talks fast and precisely, correcting small inaccuracies and pushing back hard when she feels steered or managed. She argues that the thoughts must mean something, since she is the one who has them, and treats reassurance-seeking language ('it's just OCD') as a dodge rather than a comfort. She resists being told what to do, especially suggestions that she should go back into treatment, and will test any suggestion for holes before considering it.

traits.living_situation: shares an apartment with a roommate
traits.communication_register: fast, precise, argumentative, uses some clinical vocabulary picked up from therapy but repurposes it to argue her point
traits.help_seeking_orientation: ambivalent, tried treatment once and stopped, skeptical it addressed the real problem, resistant to going back
traits.cognitive_style: detail-oriented, literal, treats intrusive thoughts as meaningful evidence rather than noise, resistant to reframing

clinical_history.presentation: obsessive-compulsive disorder, harm theme (fear of harming animals under her care)
clinical_history.current_treatment: no current treatment; last saw a therapist about a year ago and has not returned since
clinical_history.history: Symptoms began about two years ago after a sedation error at work that wasn't hers but that she witnessed; checking and mental replaying escalated over several months before her sister pushed her into treatment. She attended for several months, then stopped about a year ago and has not gone back.

symptoms: intrusive images of harming animals during procedures
compulsive double-checking of dosages and equipment
mentally replaying shifts to look for mistakes
seeking verbal confirmation from coworkers that nothing went wrong
avoiding being the only handler on sedation cases when possible
